sources.citation: ISO 639-3 Registration Authority. 2019. Change Request Number 2019-028: retire [cdg] Chamari (adopted 2020-01-23). SIL International.
sources.note: Nothing; sec. 3 retires cdg because 'There is no evidence that the language exists': 'Hammarstrom (2015) states that the Chamari [cdg] entry describes the Chamaar caste, but the Chamari do not have a language of their own.. Chamar is a caste name for skin and hide workers, with members throughout India who speak different languages (Singh 1995).'

sources.citation: Hammarström, Harald. 2015. Ethnologue 16/17/18th editions: A comprehensive review: Online appendices. Language 91(3): s1-s188 (entry on Chamari [cdg]).
sources.access_detail: open copy posted by the author (located 2026-09-25); a digital copy (available on request)
sources.locator: Online appendices, Appendix B.3 'Spurious Languages; Eurasia', printed page s55
sources.note: The only mention of Chamari in the work. It is a one-sentence spurious-language ruling: the Ethnologue Chamari [cdg] entry describes the Chamar caste, not a language. Nothing on stress, accent or tone. The cited source is Russell, R. V., and Hiralal. 1916d. 'Chamar'. Tribes and castes of the central provinces of India, vol. II, 403-423. London: Macmillan (bibliography of the appendices). Primary published argument that Chamari [cdg] is a caste entry with no language of its own; would only confirm the spurious status, not supply a stress statement.

sources.citation: Russell, R. V. & Hira Lal. 1916. Chamar. In: The Tribes and Castes of the Central Provinces of India, vol. II, 403-423. London: Macmillan. (Project Gutenberg #22010 plain text)
sources.note: Nothing; purely ethnographic caste article (divisions, marriage, funeral, religion, occupation). Only language-related remark: Chamars 'are found in most of the Hindi-speaking Districts' of the Central Provinces. No Chamari language described.
